objetivo.en: Read a e i o u as short, pure sounds and read your first Spanish words and sentences.

texto.en: Hi! I'm Lumo. Spanish is easy to read: every letter has one sound, and the vowels never change. Let's start with a and e.
The red a sounds like the a in father, but shorter and crisper. Mamá means mom.
The green e sounds like the e in bed: short and clean. Never "ay" and never "ee". Mesa means table.

pregunta.en: Which word has the e of bed?

titulo.en: The I, the O and the U

texto.en: The pink i sounds like the ee in see, but shorter. Pino means pine tree.
The orange o is the o in go, but with no w glide at the end: short and pure. Oso means bear.
The purple u sounds like the oo in moon, but shorter. It is never "yoo" like the u in English music. Uva means grape.

pregunta.en: Which word has the o of go?
Which word has the oo of moon?

texto.en: English vowels often slide into a second sound: say "no" and your lips close into a w. Spanish vowels hold still. One vowel, one sound, from start to finish.
Say it short and steady: "noh", not "now".
The e in me is "meh", like the e in bed. It is not "mee" as in English me. The sound "mee" is written mi.

pregunta.en: Which word has the ee of see?
Which word has the e of bed?

texto.en: You know all five vowels, so you can already read real sentences. The consonants m, n, p, l, t and f sound very much like English. (The letters s, c, v and d have a lesson of their own in unit 3.) The little accent marks (á, é) do not change the vowel sound; you will learn them in unit 4. Tap any word to hear it.
You just read your first sentences in Spanish! Next come the letters that surprise English speakers.

objetivo.en: Read h (silent), j and ge/gi (a strong h), ll and y (like the y in yes) and ñ (like the ny in canyon).

texto.en: Here is a surprise: in Spanish the letter h is always silent. You will see it in gray.
The h in hola is silent. Say "oh-la" and you are perfect. Hola means hello.

titulo.en: J and soft G: a strong h

texto.en: The Spanish j is like the h in the English word hat, but stronger, with a little scrape at the back of your throat. Think of it as "a strong h". Do not say it like the j in jet.
The yellow j is the strong h. Say "hee-RAH-fah" with a scratchy h. Jirafa means giraffe.
The letter g before e or i makes the same strong h: gente (people), gelatina, girasol. Before a, o and u the g is different; that comes in the next unit.

pregunta.en: Which word has the strong h?
Which word has the strong h?

texto.en: The letters ll and y both sound like the y in yes. The ll is one sound, not two l sounds.
The blue ll sounds like the y in yes: "YAH-veh". Llave means key.
A y at the start of a word is also like the y in yes: yo (I), ya (already), yoga.
Alone or at the end of a word, y is just the vowel i (like ee in see): y means and, hoy means today, muy means very.

pregunta.en: Which word has the y of yes?

texto.en: The ñ is its own letter: an n with a little wave on top. It sounds like the ny in canyon, in one smooth sound.
The ñ in piña sounds like the ny in canyon: "PEE-nya". Piña means pineapple.
Great work! You now read the letters that look strange: the silent h, the strong j, the ll and the ñ.

objetivo.en: Read the two r sounds, c/z/s and k, b and v, the soft d, and the hard and soft g.

titulo.en: R: a tap and a trill

texto.en: Spanish has two r sounds. First, the single r in the middle or end of a word: one quick tap of the tongue, like the tt in American butter or the dd in ladder.
The brown r in pera is a quick tap, like the tt in butter: "PE-ra". Your tongue touches the ridge behind your upper teeth, just once.
The second sound is a trill: your tongue vibrates, like a motor or a purring cat. You write it rr between vowels. A single r at the start of a word is also a trill.
The indigo rr is the trill. Perro means dog. If the trill is hard for you, start with a long, strong tap.
A single r after n, l or s is also a trill: Enrique, alrededor, Israel.

pregunta.en: Which word has the single tap?

texto.en: Good news: in Latin America the letters z, s, and c before e or i all make the same s sound. (In most of Spain, c and z sound like th. We use the Latin American way, the one you will hear in Ecuador.)
The s in sol sounds like the s in sun. Sol means sun.
The c before e or i is also s: cena (dinner), cine (movies), cielo (sky), cereza (cherry).
The z is s, too: zapato (shoe), zorro (fox), taza (cup), azul (blue).
The c before a, o and u is a k: casa, coco, cuchara. And qu before e or i is also k, with a silent u: queso, parque.
The two letters ch make one sound, like the ch in cheese. Do not confuse it with c plus h: the h is only silent when it stands alone. Chocolate, leche, mucho.

pregunta.en: Which word has the ch of cheese?
Which word has the s sound?
Which word has the k sound?

titulo.en: B, V and the soft D

texto.en: Another gift: b and v sound exactly the same in Spanish. Both are like an English b, a bit softer between vowels. Never put your teeth on your lip for a v.
The v in vaca sounds like the b in bebé: lips together. Vaca means cow.

nota.en: Both letters sound the same. To tell them apart, many people say "be larga" for b and "ve corta" for v.

texto.en: At the start of a word the d is like an English d. Between vowels it is softer, like the th in this: "DE-tho". Dedo means finger.

pregunta.en: Which word has the b sound?
Which word has the d sound?

texto.en: The letter g has two sounds. Before e or i it is the strong h you already know. Before a, o and u it is the g of go.
The slate g in gato is the g in go. Gato means cat.
To get the hard g before e or i, Spanish writes gu and the u stays silent: guitarra, guerra, Miguel.
If you see two dots over the u (ü), then the u is pronounced: "peen-GWEE-no". Pingüino means penguin.

pregunta.en: Which word has the g of go?
Which word has the strong h?

t.en: Emma gives bread to the dog.

texto.en: You now know every tricky consonant in Spanish! Next: which syllable to say louder.
